purpose: Independent practice of D1.1 — sorting by one rule. Used as Lesson 1 consolidation artifact and as evidence for the diagnostic checklist.
student_learning_goal: I can sort things by one rule and say what the rule is.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can sort things by one rule and say what the rule is.
header.character_watermark: Detective Dot the Sorting Squirrel in the top-right corner of the header, holding a magnifying glass. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at the pile. Sort by COLOUR. Draw each object in the right pile.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page shows a 'pile' of 8 objects scattered (4 red + 4 blue mix of shapes). Below the pile, two empty bordered boxes labelled 'RED PILE' and 'BLUE PILE' for the child to draw or place each object.

image_placeholders.description: A scatter pile of 8 mixed objects in B&W line art for a Grade 1 worksheet. Objects: 2 red squares, 2 red circles, 2 blue squares, 2 blue circles. Each object ~1in across, scattered loosely in a ~5in × 2in pile area at the top. Below the pile, two empty bordered boxes side by side labelled 'RED PILE' and 'BLUE PILE', each ~3in × 2in, for sorting.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_PILE at Part 1: instructions ask the child to sort by colour. Keywords name the visual (pile), the two colours (red, blue), and the sorting rule (colour).

parts.answer_key: RED PILE: 4 red objects (2 squares + 2 circles). BLUE PILE: 4 blue objects (2 squares + 2 circles).

parts.part_title: Part 2: Same pile, NEW rule. Sort by SHAPE.
parts.student_instructions: Same pile as Part 1. Now sort by SHAPE. Draw the squares and circles in the right pile.
parts.visual_layout: Two empty bordered boxes labelled 'SQUARES' and 'CIRCLES'. The child re-sorts the same 8 objects by shape this time.

image_placeholders.description: Two empty bordered boxes side by side for a Grade 1 worksheet. Each box ~3in × 2in with thin solid border. Labels above: 'SQUARES' (left) and 'CIRCLES' (right). Designed for the child to re-sort the same Part 1 pile by shape rule.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_BOXES at Part 2: instructions ask the child to sort by shape. Keywords name the two shapes (squares, circles) and the sorting rule (shape).

parts.answer_key: SQUARES: 4 squares (2 red + 2 blue). CIRCLES: 4 circles (2 red + 2 blue).

parts.student_instructions: Pick a rule. Sort 6 objects from your classroom. Draw and write your RULE.
parts.visual_layout: A blank rectangle (~5in × 3in) for drawing the sorted piles. Above the rectangle, a label line: 'My RULE is: ___'.

image_placeholders.description: A blank workspace rectangle ~5in × 3in for a Grade 1 worksheet, with thin solid border. Above the rectangle, a labelled line reading 'My RULE is: ___'. Designed for the child to write their rule and then draw their sorted piles inside the box.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_FRAME at Part 3: instructions ask the child to pick their own rule and sort. Keywords name the activity (rule, sort).

parts.answer_key: Any valid rule and sorted piles. Common: rule = colour (sorts crayons), rule = laces (sorts shoes), rule = animal (sorts toys). Accept any sort that consistently follows the named rule.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, sort the SAME 6 objects by a DIFFERENT rule. What changes?
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation artifact. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 with one prompt. For Part 3, accept any rule that the child can articulate. Use Part 1 + 2 as the primary diagnostic signal — children who succeed at re-sorting the same pile by a NEW rule have grasped the 'rule decides' concept.
